title: Bug: music plays way too fast + clips (per-frame chunk submit)
description: audio_update() submits a ~33ms music chunk every frame; at >30fps this pushes music faster than real-time and overlapping chunks clip badly ('breaks speakers'). Fix: render the full music loop once and submit it to the backend as a single LOOPING voice (paced by the device callback); remove the per-frame music submission in audio_update.
close_reason: Fixed: music rendered once and looped by backend; audio_update no longer submits per-frame chunks. Volume/mute live via set_loop_gain. Tests added, full build + 24/24 ctest pass. Branch feat/audio-music-loopfix.

title: Debt: Unchecked thread creation in platform_thread (Win32)
description: platform_thread.h:97: pt_thread_create malloc for PT__ThreadArgs can fail without error handling. CreateThread at line 100 may also fail silently. If malloc fails, the freed pointer is still passed to CreateThread; if CreateThread fails, no error returned. Add null checks and return error status.
close_reason: pt_thread_create returns int; Win32 checks malloc'd arg and CreateThread, POSIX checks pthread_create; net_thread_start propagates failure.

Store in World struct (already done). File: src/main.c:281 (hardcoded to 8, needs parameterization), src/world.c:273-280 (already supports parameter)

title: Bug: save/load doesn't show edits on reload (two-worlds)

Root cause: persistence overlay is applied only to the SERVER world at chunk gen, but the host client renders its own seed-generated world that never sees the overlay. Expected to be fixed by the server-authoritative world unification (host client renders the server world). Tracked against feat/world-authority.

Two-worlds divergence eliminated for singleplayer/host; save/load round-trips (per 0w8 notes).

title: Server world authority: on-demand chunk gen for validation + send persisted overlay on join

close_reason: Fixed: break validation falls back to client claim when server chunk reads AIR (async streaming).

title: Netcode: add protocol version field + connect handshake version check
description: Serialization is hand-rolled byte packing with NO version field (net.h header: type/player_id/seq/ack/ack_bits). A client/server packet-format mismatch corrupts silently. Add a protocol version constant, carry it in PKT_CONNECT_REQUEST/ACCEPT, and reject mismatched clients with a clear disconnect reason. FOUNDATION: land this before features add new packets so format drift is caught, not silently corrupting. Effort S.
close_reason: Implemented: protocol version + handshake rejection with typed disconnect reasons; net unit tests pass. On feat/netcode-version.

title: EPIC: server-authoritative chunk streaming (stop client-side regen)
description: Today the server and each client independently generate the world from the shared seed; only block-change deltas + a persistence overlay are synced. This is fragile: validation/interaction depend on the server having generated the chunk, and late joiners regenerate from seed and miss persisted edits -> divergence. Gold-standard fix: server owns chunks and STREAMS chunk data (and edits) to clients; clients stop regenerating. Needs a chunk-transfer protocol (use the reliable fragmentation already added), compression, and client-side chunk receive/apply. Large. Interim mitigation tracked separately (on-demand server gen + overlay-on-join).
notes: Host/singleplayer shared-world unification DONE + tested (one authoritative world, no double-gen, save/load round-trips). RLE chunk-wire module + wire packets (v7) DONE + tested. Remote streaming integration is PARTIAL — split to follow-up bead. Branch feat/world-authority.

title: Villages: per-chunk building generation

title: Debt: Race condition in chunk meta/lights lazy allocation
description: chunk.h:73-78,98-104: chunk_ensure_meta and chunk_ensure_lights do unlocked calloc and assign. Called from chunk_set_* inline functions which may be invoked from multiple threads (main thread block-change vs worker threads lighting). Two threads could both allocate, leak first, and create data races. Protect with atomic CAS or pre-allocate.

title: Perf: Optimize present mode (MAILBOX uses extra memory/latency vs FIFO for iGPU)
description: Swapchain prefers MAILBOX (low-latency, no frame queuing) but defaults to FIFO in swapchain.c:21-28. MAILBOX allocates triple-buffering internally. On iGPU with tight memory, FIFO (vsync with frame queue) or FIFO_RELAXED may reduce overhead. Recommendation: Add config or detect iGPU to prefer FIFO mode. File: src/swapchain.c:21-28 (present mode selection)

title: Perf: Add dynamic render scale / resolution downsampling option

title: Perf: Verify mesher uses greedy meshing (minimize vertex/index count)
description: Mesher currently emits per-face quads in mesher.c:61-98 (emit_quad). Each quad = 4 verts + 6 indices, no greedy coalescing. Verify if adjacent same-texture faces are merged (horizontal greedy meshing would reduce verts ~40%). File: src/mesher.c (emit_quad, mesh generation loop). Check: are adjacent blocks merged or each face individually emitted?

title: Perf: Batch chunk draws or use indirect rendering (reduce draw call overhead)
description: Each chunk is drawn with vkCmdDrawIndexed() per chunk in renderer_frame.c:172. With render_distance=32, ~3200 individual draw calls per frame. On iGPU, driver CPU overhead is significant. Recommendation: Batch meshes into one VB/IB per ~100 chunks, or use VK_KHR_indirect_draw for multi-draw. title: Netcode: reliable message fragmentation for payloads >256B
description: RELIABLE_MAX_PAYLOAD is 256B (reliable.h). Larger reliable messages (future inventory/crafting/chunk sync) cannot be sent. Add fragment headers (frag_id/total) and reassembly so reliable payloads up to MTU work. Effort M.
close_reason: implemented: reliable.c fragment_count/fragment_build/reassemble (RELIABLE_FRAG_* magic+header) — payloads up to RELIABLE_FRAG_MAX supported; used by chunk-wire

title: Netcode: central bounds-checked packet codec (cursor read/write)
description: Every packet has inline net_write_*/net_read_* with manual offsets; offset bugs propagate and there is no bounds checking. Add a NetCursor {buf,off,limit} with codec_write/read_* that assert against limit. Refactor existing packet builders onto it. Reduces serialization bugs as packet types grow. Effort M.

title: Netcode: sequence + dedup for unreliable broadcasts (WORLD_STATE/MOB_STATE)
description: PKT_WORLD_STATE and PKT_MOB_STATE are sent unreliable with no sequence number; an out-of-order/late packet applies stale positions over newer ones (visible rubber-banding). Add a per-stream seq to these broadcasts and have the client discard packets older than the last applied. Effort M.
close_reason: Closed

title: Server-side anti-cheat: reject implausibly fast block breaks
description: Follow-up to mine-vibe-exc (block hardness + timed mining). Mining is currently client-timed: the client accumulates block_break_time seconds before sending PKT_BLOCK_BREAK. The server validates reach + inventory but does not verify timing, so a modified client could break instantly. Enforcing this server-side needs per-client per-target mining-start tracking and likely a wire change (e.g. a PKT_BLOCK_BREAK_START) plus a NET_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump. Deferred to keep v1 low-risk and wire-stable.

title: Polish: Extract magic numbers into named constants
description:
Code contains hardcoded values that should be named for clarity:
